messages.subject: Re: [Cytoscape-discuss] Getting VizMaper to look like KEGG output.
messages.subject_clean: [Cytoscape-discuss] Getting VizMaper to look like KEGG output.
messages.body_plain:
Some of us find that RCytoscape provides a good way to manipulate the vizmapper programmatically and reproducibly -- assuming you don't mind working in R.

But if R is not your cup of tea, and maybe python is, Jan Bot's CytsocapeRPC plugin (upon which RCytoscape depends) works great with python, and Jan's tutorial gives examples of the python API:

  https://wiki.nbic.nl/index.php/File:CytoscapeRPC_tutorial.pdf

If R is of interest, read on!    To whet your appetite, a sample of a somewhat KEGG-like map is displayed prominently at

  http://rcytocape.systemsbiology.net

With RCytoscape, you can make function calls like this:

  setNodeColorRule (...)
  setDefaultNodeColor (...)
  setNodeColorDirect (...)

Layout gets easier too.  After you have created the layout you want-- via the layout menus, some manual repositioning, or your own series of 'setNodePosition' function calls, you can save that layout for later use:

   saveLayout (cw, 'someFileName')
    ... # later
   restoreLayout (cw, 'someFileName')

RCytocape 1.4.3 is a Bioconductor package, and comes with a vignette (an introduction which includes sample code) and a pretty well-stocked website

  http://rcytocape.systemsbiology.net

which includes installation instructions.

 - Paul

> KEGG and feel comfortable with it. I would like to be able to make the
> VizMapper create an output visual style that resembles a KEGG map as
> closely as possible, i.e. same colours, same shapes for nodes and
> edges, very similar looking typeface and fonts. I have been playing
> with the VizMapper's visual styles bbut not having a lot of luck. Any
> suggestions would be helpful.
>
> Thanks so much!

messages.subject: extracting node attributes in RCy [was Re: another question about RCytoscape]
messages.subject_clean: extracting node attributes in RCy [was Re: another question about RCytoscape]
messages.body_plain:
Hi Ben,

(I am taking the liberty of CC'ing the cytoscape list on this.  I trust people will let me know if this is inappropriate.)

Assuming you imported your Cytoscape network this way:

   cw = existing.CytoscapeWindow ("pdgfra & neighborhood", copy.graph.from.cytoscape.to.R=TRUE)

Then you get the graph through either of these commands

   g = cw@graph

or
    g = getGraph (cw)

Imagine, then, that you want to find out some node attribute values for a few nodes which you manually select in Cytoscape:

   getSelectedNodeCount (cw)  # [1] 3    (make sure there really are selected nodes there)
   getSelectedNodes (cw)      # [1] "1956" "5294" "5156"   (get their node ids)

   noa.names (g)              # [1] "nodeType"   "commonName" "summary"    "lfc"        "copyNumber" "mutation"   "score"

Now get the attribute you want for just the nodes you are interested in

   noa (g, 'commonName') [getSelectedNodes (cw)]   #     1956     5294     5156
                                                   #    "EGFR" "PIK3CG" "PDGFRA"

Or, more directly, naming two nodes explicitly, and using another attribute ('lfc'):

   noa (g, 'lfc') [c ('1956', '5156')]    #      1956    5156
                                          #     0.832    -1.2

Does this help?  If not, point me in the right direction; I'll try again!

 - Paul

On Jan 12, 2012, at 8:50 AM, Benjamin White wrote:

> Hi Paul,
>
> I've got another question for you re: RCytoscape.
>
> Once I've imported a network from Cytoscape into R, via g <- cw@graph, how would I go about accessing attributes for individual nodes in g (rather than individual nodes in cw).  For instance, the noa function can take a graph as its object (as opposed to a cytoscape window object), but as far as i can tell, you can only use noa to return an attribute value for all nodes in a graph. I'd like to be able to return attribute values in a graph for a specific node or set of nodes in a graph.
>
> Would I just want to port g (form g <- cw@graph) to igraph and use igraph methods (by using igraph.from.graphNEL)?  Or is there something more obvious that I'm missing?
>
> Thanks, yet again.
>
> Ben
